Register rate limit cannot be bypassed by spoofed X-Forwarded-For (verified). critical.issue: Admin's live bot (Dev_nara_bot) webhook is still registered at .../api/webhooks/telegram/8605848445 (old URL scheme using bot id, not business_id). Current route treats '8605848445' as bid -> get_settings returns defaults (no token) -> every Telegram update gets 403. Telegram for the existing admin business is silently broken after the multi-tenant migration. /api/channels/status still reports connected:true because it only checks that webhook url is non-empty.

minor.issue: telegram.connected should verify getWebhookInfo.url == f'{base}/api/webhooks/telegram/{bid}' (and optionally last_error_message), otherwise a stale/wrong webhook is shown as connected.

Old /api/public/chat, /api/public/info, /api/webhooks/messenger (no bid) now 404. Any Meta app already configured with the old callback URL stops receiving messages; consider keeping legacy aliases mapped to the default business or forcing reconnect.

LLM returned summary in Chinese for an English-only conversation (big-inbox 'Customer #2601': 'Do you sell coffee beans to take home?'). Make the language instruction explicit (detect from customer messages / pass settings.language) in SUMMARY_PROMPT.

In-memory per-process; resets on restart and is not shared across replicas/workers. Register limit 5/hour per IP also counts failed (duplicate-email) attempts, so a shared office/NAT IP can be blocked from signing up after a few typos.
Cursor uses updated_at $lt only; conversations with identical updated_at at a page boundary would be skipped. No ties in current data, but use (updated_at, id) compound cursor for robustness.

ui_bugs.issue: /embed?b=<unknown-bid> shows an empty widget with repeated 'Unhandled rejection: Request failed with status code 404' (info + history polling not caught). Should show a friendly 'Chat unavailable' state and stop polling.
Owner visiting /dashboard/businesses (or any unknown /dashboard/* path) gets a blank content area; add a catch-all <Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='/dashboard' />} />.

integration_issues.issue: Conversation list keeps its scroll position when changing filter/search; the scroll handler can fire loadMore with a 'before' cursor from the previous list (observed telegram filter showing 67 items instead of 50 right after switching). No gaps observed, but reset scrollTop to 0 on filter/q change and ignore stale loadMore responses.

issues: embed-code box overflows its column and the section divider on 1920px (long single-line code; extends past the content width). Use break-all / overflow-x-auto.
Chats/AI replies cells not formatted (3000 vs stat card 3,106) - use toLocaleString().
Business name (dash-business-name) not visible on mobile top bar; owners of multiple accounts can't tell which business they are in.

critical_code_review_comments: telegram_webhook/messenger_* do not check business exists (fine, returns 403) but two businesses saving the same Telegram token would hijack each other's webhook - consider uniqueness check on telegram_token.
PUT /settings has no role check: Google team 'member' users can change tokens, allowed_emails and business name. Consider owner-only for channel tokens/team.
google_login joins the first settings doc containing the email in allowed_emails; if multiple businesses list the same email the choice is arbitrary.
Opening any conversation auto-triggers an LLM summary after 1.5s (cost scales with inbox browsing in large inboxes).
admin_businesses aggregates all messages each call and caps at 5000 businesses with no pagination.
Old test suites still reference non-bid messenger webhook URLs and list-shaped /api/conversations; superseded by test_iter4_multitenant.py.

rca of the issue: Telegram: pre-migration code registered the webhook as /api/webhooks/telegram/<bot id prefix of token>. Migration (migrate_single_tenant) moved settings into a new business but never called setWebhook again; new route /webhooks/telegram/{bid} looks up settings by bid='8605848445' -> no settings -> empty token -> 403 'Bad secret'. Reproduce: curl https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getWebhookInfo -> url ends with /8605848445. Fix: on startup, for each settings with telegram_token, call setWebhook(url=.../telegram/{business_id}, secret_token=tg_secret(bid, token)) (needs public base URL) or prompt reconnect; tighten channels_status check.
